description: CAL-3 calibration input: free-neutron β-decay Q-value Q_β(n). Per the QOU three-calibration discipline (folio/quantum-observable-universe/braids-and-knots/three-calibration-inputs.md), Q_β(n) is one of exactly three external inputs to the framework — alongside m_e (CAL-1) and m_μ/m_e (CAL-2) — used to fix the hadronic energy scale E_0 via E_0 = Q_β(n) / |Δ(net)|, where Δ(net) = h(h-2)/2 is the symbolic NF difference between neutron and proton braids. This witness exists so codata_constants.py loads the CAL-3 value from a source-of-truth JSON instead of hardcoding it. Q_β here is the PRIMARY DEFINITION of the input; it must agree (within combined CODATA σ) with the algebraic identity m_n - m_p - m_e computed from the validation witness, but that identity is a CONSISTENCY CHECK, not the definition.

parameters.role: Hadronic energy scale E_0 via E_0 = Q_β(n) / |Δ(net)|
parameters.data_source: PDG 2024 free-neutron β-decay Q-value (n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e), consistent with AME 2020 mass-difference computation. Sourced from codata_2022_source.Q_BETA_MEV_AME.

downstream_consumers: neutron-gap-probes-round3.witness.json 3-input mass split: m_n_pred = m_p_pred + Q_β + m_e

q0AnchorReason: CAL-3 tabulates the experimental PDG 2024 / AME 2020 free-neutron beta-decay Q-value from codata_2022_source; no substrate q_0 is read.
